title: California newsroom replaces dozens of laid-off reporters with AI writers
text:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

McClatchy Media is cutting journalists at several California newspapers while building a new artificial intelligence operation that could dramatically change what its newsrooms produce.

The newspaper giant laid off dozens of reporters nationwide last week, then added three editors to its AI-powered Content Innovation Lab.

The company’s AI strategy was already being pushed internally months before the latest cuts.

During a contentious May virtual town hall, CEO Tony Hunter delivered a blunt pitch for the company’s future.

“We have a company-wide effort to agentify the entire enterprise,”  Hunter said in a recording obtained by Straight Arrow News.

That effort includes a chatbot that repackages human-written stories at different lengths for different audiences, complete with reporters’ bylines.

McClatchy executives have described the Content Innovation Lab as a “big experiment” and claim AI can help them produce and scale more content while experimenting with new audiences, even as the number of traditional newsroom employees is reduced.

But the strategy is colliding with a painful reality in California, where some of the company’s most recognizable newsrooms have already been gutted by layoffs.

The Fresno Bee lost seven reporters, while The Sacramento Bee lost at least 10 journalists. The Modesto Bee was also hit, with cuts affecting not only reporters but photographers and videographers.

Kathleen Quinn, a civics and democracy reporter for The Modesto Bee, announced that she had been laid off after two years with the company.

“To say I’m extremely disappointed in McClatchy Media doesn’t really scratch the surface of what I feel knowing how many incredibly talented people were laid off today in some of the most critical positions in our industry,” she wrote. “Please hire these folks.”

Sacramento Bee investigative reporter Ariane Lange described the cuts as “the bloodiest round of layoffs in quite some time at McClatchy.”

The losses come as California communities continue to face the same shrinking-newsroom problem affecting local papers nationwide: fewer reporters to cover city halls, schools, public agencies and other institutions.

And McClatchy’s own job listing makes clear that AI is central to the company’s strategy. The listing says the “company’s future depends” on embracing AI and describes the innovation lab as its “next-generation approach to content” designed to “fuel experimentation and productivity.”

The shift has sparked concern inside the company.

A Kansas City Star reporter who survived the layoffs called the new innovation lab positions “AI content farm jobs” and accused McClatchy of prioritizing AI-generated lifestyle content over local coverage.
